summary.name: Treatment-Linked BMP Scheduling
summary.description: Evaluate the Monitoring Plan using the selected treatment action and kidney disease status. Branch conditions mirror Decision Table 2 without assuming undocumented fields of its composite output. The human review tasks require an authorized reviewer to order and arrange the BMP for the applicable interval after medication initiation; review alone does not complete these tasks. The clinicians group is an authorization binding, not a source-specified ordering or scheduling actor. Lifestyle-only treatment creates no additional routine BMP under Table 2. Baseline testing and standard preventive care remain unaffected.

source.source_text: Patients initiating medication therapy require laboratory monitoring to assess for potential adverse effects, particularly in patients with pre-existing kidney disease.

parameters.description: Maximum duration of this automation, distinct from laboratory timing after medication initiation.

automatability.rationale: The source describes a repeatable operational sequence with explicit timing or trigger: Medication initiation anchors laboratory timing, CKD: 2 weeks, No CKD: 4 weeks.
